task: Develop and validate a universal foundation model for atomistic simulations (MACE-MP-0)
method: MACE higher-order equivariant message passing neural network trained on MPtrj dataset (~1.5M structures)
validation_experiments: Experiment 1: Liquid water RDF simulation (32 H2O, 330K, Langevin MD)
Experiment 2: Adsorption energy scaling relations on fcc(111) transition metal surfaces (Ni, Cu, Rh, Pd, Ir, Pt)
Experiment 3: CRBH20 reaction barrier comparison (3 reactions)
key_findings: MACE-MP-0 produces stable liquid water MD and captures RDF features
Linear scaling relations between O* and OH* adsorption energies are recovered (R²=0.96 excl. Ni)
Reaction barriers from simplified geometries show qualitative trends but limited quantitative accuracy
Foundation model demonstrates broad transferability across liquids, surfaces, and reactions
limitations: CPU-only computation limited MD trajectory length
Simplified reaction geometries (not fully relaxed TS) limit barrier accuracy
Ni adsorption outlier suggests model uncertainty for certain surface chemistries
Fine-tuning on task-specific data recommended for quantitative accuracy
